records.literal_gloss: And went out Jehoiachin king of Judah to [the] king of Babylon, he and his mother and his servants and his princes and his eunuchs; and took him [the] king of Babylon in [the] year eight of his reigning.

en.L: And Jehoiachin king of Judah went out to the king of Babylon, he and his mother and his servants and his princes and his eunuchs; and the king of Babylon took him in [the] eighth year of his reign.
en.B: Jehoiachin king of Judah went out to the king of Babylon in surrender, he and his mother, his servants, his officials and his court officers. The king of Babylon took him prisoner in the eighth year of his reign.
en.R: Jehoiachin king of Judah surrendered to the king of Babylon. He went out to him with his mother, his servants, his leaders and his palace officials. The king of Babylon took him prisoner. It was the eighth year that Nebuchadnezzar had been king.

es.L: Y salió Joaquín, rey de Judá, al rey de Babilonia, él y su madre, y sus siervos, y sus príncipes y sus eunucos; y el rey de Babilonia lo tomó en el año octavo de su reinado.
es.B: Joaquín, rey de Judá, salió a rendirse ante el rey de Babilonia, junto con su madre, sus siervos, sus funcionarios y los oficiales de su corte. El rey de Babilonia lo tomó prisionero en el octavo año de su reinado.
es.R: Joaquín, rey de Judá, se rindió ante el rey de Babilonia. Salió a su encuentro con su madre, sus siervos, sus jefes y los funcionarios de su palacio. El rey de Babilonia lo tomó prisionero. Era el octavo año del reinado de Nabucodonosor.

fr.L: Et Joïakin, roi de Juda, sortit vers le roi de Babylone, lui, sa mère, ses serviteurs, ses princes et ses eunuques ; et le roi de Babylone le prit en la huitième année de son règne.
fr.B: Joïakin, roi de Juda, se rendit au roi de Babylone, avec sa mère, ses serviteurs, ses chefs et ses hauts fonctionnaires. Le roi de Babylone le fit prisonnier la huitième année de son règne.
fr.R: Joïakin, roi de Juda, s’est rendu au roi de Babylone. Il est sorti vers lui avec sa mère, ses serviteurs, ses chefs et les fonctionnaires du palais. Le roi de Babylone l’a fait prisonnier. C’était la huitième année du règne de Nabuchodonosor.

sw.L: Naye Yehoyakini mfalme wa Yuda akatoka kwenda kwa mfalme wa Babeli, yeye na mama yake na watumishi wake na wakuu wake na matowashi wake; naye mfalme wa Babeli akamchukua katika mwaka wa nane wa kutawala kwake.
sw.B: Yehoyakini mfalme wa Yuda alitoka kwenda kujisalimisha kwa mfalme wa Babeli, yeye na mama yake, watumishi wake, maafisa wake na wakuu wa ikulu yake. Mfalme wa Babeli akamchukua mateka katika mwaka wa nane wa utawala wake.
sw.R: Yehoyakini mfalme wa Yuda alijisalimisha kwa mfalme wa Babeli. Alitoka kwenda kwake pamoja na mama yake, watumishi wake, viongozi wake na maafisa wa jumba lake. Mfalme wa Babeli akamchukua mateka. Ilikuwa katika mwaka wa nane wa utawala wa Nebukadneza.

vi.L: Giê-hô-gia-kin vua Giu-đa đi ra đến vua Ba-by-lôn, ông cùng mẹ ông, các đầy tớ, các thủ lĩnh và các hoạn quan của ông; vua Ba-by-lôn bắt ông vào năm thứ tám đời trị vì của vua ấy.
vi.B: Giê-hô-gia-kin vua Giu-đa ra đầu hàng vua Ba-by-lôn, cùng với mẹ vua, các đầy tớ, các quan chức và các triều thần của vua. Vua Ba-by-lôn bắt Giê-hô-gia-kin làm tù binh vào năm thứ tám đời trị vì của mình.
vi.R: Giê-hô-gia-kin vua Giu-đa đầu hàng vua Ba-by-lôn. Ông ra gặp vua ấy cùng với mẹ mình, các đầy tớ, các thủ lĩnh và các quan chức trong cung. Vua Ba-by-lôn bắt ông làm tù binh. Lúc ấy là năm thứ tám đời Nê-bu-cát-nết-sa làm vua.

ko.L: 그리고 유다 왕 여호야긴이 그와 그의 어머니와 그의 신하들과 그의 고관들과 그의 내시들과 함께 바빌론 왕에게 나갔다. 그리고 바빌론 왕이 그의 통치 제8년에 그를 사로잡았다.
ko.B: 유다 왕 여호야긴은 그의 어머니와 신하들과 고관들과 관리들과 함께 바빌론 왕에게 나가 항복했다. 바빌론 왕은 자기가 다스린 지 8년째 되는 해에 그를 사로잡았다.
ko.R: 유다 왕 여호야긴은 바빌론 왕에게 항복했다. 그는 자기 어머니와 신하들과 지도자들과 왕궁 관리들을 데리고 바빌론 왕에게 나갔다. 바빌론 왕은 그를 포로로 잡았다. 그때는 느부갓네살이 왕이 된 지 8년째 되는 해였다.

pt.L: E Joaquim, rei de Judá, saiu ao rei da Babilônia, ele, e a sua mãe, e os seus servos, e os seus príncipes, e os seus eunucos; e o rei da Babilônia o tomou no oitavo ano do seu reinado.
pt.B: Joaquim, rei de Judá, saiu e se rendeu ao rei da Babilônia, ele, a sua mãe, os seus servos, os seus oficiais e os funcionários da corte. O rei da Babilônia o fez prisioneiro no oitavo ano do seu reinado.
pt.R: Joaquim, rei de Judá, se rendeu ao rei da Babilônia. Ele saiu ao encontro dele com a sua mãe, os seus servos, os seus líderes e os oficiais do palácio. O rei da Babilônia o fez prisioneiro. Era o oitavo ano do reinado de Nabucodonosor.

am.L: የይሁዳም ንጉሥ ዮአኪን እርሱና እናቱ፣ ባሪያዎቹም፣ አለቆቹም፣ ጃንደረቦቹም ወደ ባቢሎን ንጉሥ ወጡ፤ የባቢሎንም ንጉሥ በነገሠ በስምንተኛው ዓመት ያዘው።
am.B: የይሁዳ ንጉሥ ዮአኪን ከእናቱ፣ ከአገልጋዮቹ፣ ከመኳንንቱና ከቤተ መንግሥቱ ሹማምንት ጋር ወጥቶ ለባቢሎን ንጉሥ እጁን ሰጠ። የባቢሎን ንጉሥም በነገሠ በስምንተኛው ዓመት ማረከው።
am.R: የይሁዳ ንጉሥ ዮአኪን ለባቢሎን ንጉሥ እጁን ሰጠ። ከእናቱ፣ ከአገልጋዮቹ፣ ከመሪዎቹና ከቤተ መንግሥቱ ሹማምንት ጋር ወደ እርሱ ወጣ። የባቢሎን ንጉሥም ማረከው። ይህም ናቡከደነፆር በነገሠ በስምንተኛው ዓመት ነበር።

hi.L: और यहूदा का राजा यहोयाकीन बाबुल के राजा के पास बाहर निकल गया, वह और उसकी माता और उसके दास और उसके हाकिम और उसके खोजे; और बाबुल के राजा ने उसे अपने राज्य के आठवें वर्ष में पकड़ लिया।
hi.B: यहूदा का राजा यहोयाकीन हथियार डालकर बाबुल के राजा के पास बाहर आया, वह और उसकी माता, उसके अधिकारी, उसके हाकिम और उसके दरबारी। बाबुल के राजा ने अपने राज्य के आठवें वर्ष में उसे बंदी बना लिया।
hi.R: यहूदा के राजा यहोयाकीन ने बाबुल के राजा के सामने हथियार डाल दिए। वह अपनी माता, अपने अधिकारियों, अपने अगुवों और अपने महल के कर्मचारियों के साथ उसके पास बाहर गया। बाबुल के राजा ने उसे बंदी बना लिया। यह नबूकदनेस्सर के राज्य का आठवाँ वर्ष था।

ru.L: И вышел Иехония, царь Иуды, к царю Вавилона, он, и его мать, и его рабы, и его князья, и его евнухи; и взял его царь Вавилона в восьмой год своего царствования.
ru.B: Иехония, царь Иуды, вышел и сдался царю Вавилона — он сам, его мать, его приближённые, вельможи и придворные. Царь Вавилона взял его в плен в восьмой год своего царствования.
ru.R: Иехония, царь Иуды, сдался царю Вавилона. Он вышел к нему вместе со своей матерью, приближёнными, начальниками и придворными. Царь Вавилона взял его в плен. Это был восьмой год царствования Навуходоносора.

ja.L: そしてユダの王ヨヤキンは、彼と、彼の母と、彼の家臣たちと、彼の高官たちと、彼の宦官たちとで、バビロンの王のもとに出て行った。そしてバビロンの王は、その治世の第八年に彼を捕らえた。
ja.B: ユダの王ヨヤキンは、母、家臣たち、高官たち、宮廷の役人たちと共に、自らバビロンの王のもとに出て行って降伏した。バビロンの王は、治世第八年に彼を捕らえた。
ja.R: ユダの王ヨヤキンは、バビロンの王に降伏しました。母や家来たち、指導者たち、王宮の役人たちと一緒に、バビロンの王のところへ出て行ったのです。バビロンの王はヨヤキンを捕虜にしました。それは、ネブカドネツァルが王になって八年目のことでした。

uk.L: І вийшов Єгояхин, цар Юдеї, до царя Вавилону, він, і його мати, і його раби, і його князі, і його євнухи; і взяв його цар Вавилону у восьмому році свого царювання.
uk.B: Єгояхин, цар Юдеї, вийшов здатися цареві Вавилону, він, і його мати, і його слуги, і його вельможі, і його придворні. Цар Вавилону взяв його в полон у восьмому році свого царювання.
uk.R: Єгояхин, цар Юдеї, здався цареві Вавилону. Він вийшов до нього разом зі своєю матірʼю, слугами, провідниками і палацовими урядовцями. Цар Вавилону взяв його в полон. Це був восьмий рік царювання Навуходоносора.

decisions.choice: went out to the king of Babylon: surrendered
decisions.reason: To go out of a besieged city to the enemy king is to give oneself up to him (18:31; 1 Samuel 11:3). Jehoiachin came out with his whole court.

decisions.choice: eunuchs: royal officials, perhaps castrated men
decisions.reason: The word names a class of court officers. Many of them in the courts of the ancient Near East were castrated, but the word is also used of high officials who were not, so it may simply mean "palace officials" here.

decisions.choice: the eighth year of his reign: Nebuchadnezzar's eighth year, 597 BC
decisions.reason: "His" is the king of Babylon. Babylon's own records of the period date the capture of Jerusalem to early 597 BC. Jeremiah 52:28 dates a deportation to Nebuchadnezzar's seventh year; that list may count the years from a different starting point, or describe another group.

decisions.choice: took him: the start of Jehoiachin's long captivity
decisions.reason: Jehoiachin stayed a prisoner in Babylon for thirty-seven years, until a later king of Babylon released him (25:27-30).

decisions.choice: servants, princes, eunuchs (Literal); servants, officials, court officers (Balanced); servants, leaders, palace officials (Readable)
decisions.reason: Three words for the king's court stand side by side here. Literal follows the usual wording for each. Balanced uses "officials" for the princes as usual, so it calls the eunuchs "court officers" to keep the three groups apart; Readable has "leaders" for the princes and "palace officials" for the eunuchs.

decisions.choice: in surrender; took him prisoner
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what going out to the enemy and being taken meant. Readable names Nebuchadnezzar so that "his reign" is clear.

decisions.choice: "siervos, príncipes, eunucos" (L); "siervos, funcionarios, oficiales de su corte" (B); "siervos, jefes, funcionarios de su palacio" (R)
decisions.reason: Three words for the king's court stand side by side; each level keeps them apart as the English does, with "eunucos" at Literal as the terms note sets.

decisions.choice: "eunuques" (L); "hauts fonctionnaires" (B); "fonctionnaires du palais" (R)
decisions.reason: *Sarisim* as the terms note sets for royal officials (m2).

decisions.choice: watumishi, wakuu, matowashi (Literal); watumishi, maafisa, wakuu wa ikulu (Balanced); watumishi, viongozi, maafisa wa jumba (Readable)
decisions.reason: The court in the terms note's wording: *sarisim* are "matowashi" at Literal and court officials at Balanced and Readable.

decisions.choice: servos, príncipes, eunucos (L); servos, oficiais, funcionários da corte (B); servos, líderes, oficiais do palácio (R); no oitavo ano do seu reinado
decisions.reason: The three words for the court keep one Portuguese word each at each level, as the English does: "eunucos" at Literal as 23:11, "funcionários da corte" at Balanced so as not to repeat "oficiais", used for the princes. The year (m3) is an ordinal, "oitavo", as the synchronisms of the book give it (1 Kings 15:1).

decisions.choice: "went out to the king of Babylon" is "ወጥቶ … እጁን ሰጠ" (surrendered).
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads going out to the besieger as surrender; "እጁን ሰጠ" is the Amharic idiom for it, while Literal keeps the bare verb.

decisions.choice: दास, हाकिम, खोजे (L); अधिकारी, हाकिम, दरबारी (B); अधिकारी, अगुवे, महल के कर्मचारी (R)
decisions.reason: Three words for the king's court stand side by side, so each level keeps them apart: Literal with its usual words (खोजा as at 23:11), Balanced and Readable with the words they use elsewhere for servants (अधिकारी) and princes, and a third word for the eunuchs.

decisions.choice: "рабы, князья, евнухи" (L); "приближённые, вельможи, придворные" (B); "приближённые, начальники, придворные" (R)
decisions.reason: Three words for the court stand side by side. Each level keeps its usual word for the king's servants ("рабы" at Literal, "приближённые" at Balanced and Readable, as 2 Samuel and 1 Kings) and for the eunuchs ("евнух" at Literal, "придворный" at Balanced and Readable, as 1 Kings 22:9), and finds a third for the princes.

decisions.choice: "царь Иуды" (every level)
decisions.reason: "King of Judah" in running narrative is "царь Иуды" at every level, as 1 Kings 22:2 sets; the dating formulas keep the adjective of the history note.

decisions.choice: "家臣たち、高官たち、宦官たち" (L); "家臣たち、高官たち、宮廷の役人たち" (B); "家来たち、指導者たち、王宮の役人たち" (R)
decisions.reason: saris as at 23:11: Literal keeps the word, Balanced and Readable name the office, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "出て行って降伏した" / "捕らえた" (B); "降伏しました" / "捕虜にしました" (R)
decisions.reason: Going out to the besieger means surrender.

source.text: וַיּוֹצֵ֣א מִשָּׁ֗ם אֶת־כָּל־אוֹצְרוֹת֙ בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֔ה וְאֽוֹצְר֖וֹת בֵּ֣ית הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיְקַצֵּ֞ץ אֶת־כָּל־כְּלֵ֣י הַזָּהָ֗ב אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשָׂ֜ה שְׁלֹמֹ֤ה מֶֽלֶךְ־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ בְּהֵיכַ֣ל יְהוָ֔ה כַּֽאֲשֶׁ֖ר דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And he brought out from there all [the] treasures of [the] house of Yahweh and [the] treasures of [the] house of the king, and he cut up all [the] vessels of the gold which had made Solomon king of Israel in [the] temple of Yahweh, as had spoken Yahweh.

en.L: And he brought out from there all the treasures of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and the treasures of the house of the king, and he cut up all the vessels of gold that Solomon king of Israel had made in the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had spoken.
en.B: He carried off from there all the treasures of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and those of the king's palace, and he cut up all the gold vessels that Solomon king of Israel had made for the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said.
en.R: Nebuchadnezzar took away all the treasures from the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and from the king's palace. He cut into pieces all the gold objects that Solomon king of Israel had made for the temple. This was just what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said would happen.

es.L: Y sacó de allí todos los tesoros de la casa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} y los tesoros de la casa del rey, y despedazó todos los utensilios de oro que había hecho Salomón, rey de Israel, en el templo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, como {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} había dicho.
es.B: Se llevó de allí todos los tesoros de la casa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} y los del palacio real, y despedazó todos los utensilios de oro que Salomón, rey de Israel, había hecho para el templo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, tal como {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} lo había anunciado.
es.R: Nabucodonosor se llevó todos los tesoros del templo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} y del palacio real. Hizo pedazos todos los objetos de oro que Salomón, rey de Israel, había hecho para el templo. Así sucedió lo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} había dicho que pasaría.

fr.L: Et il emporta de là tous les trésors de la maison {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} et les trésors de la maison du roi, et il mit en pièces tous les objets d’or qu’avait faits Salomon, roi d’Israël, dans le temple {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, comme {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} l’avait dit.
fr.B: Il emporta de là tous les trésors de la maison {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} et ceux du palais royal, et il mit en pièces tous les objets d’or que Salomon, roi d’Israël, avait faits pour le temple {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, comme {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} l’avait annoncé.
fr.R: Nabuchodonosor a emporté tous les trésors du temple {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} et du palais du roi. Il a cassé en morceaux tous les objets en or que Salomon, roi d’Israël, avait fabriqués pour le temple. C’est exactement ce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} avait annoncé.

sw.L: Naye akatoa huko hazina zote za nyumba ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na hazina za nyumba ya mfalme, akavikatakata vyombo vyote vya dhahabu ambavyo Sulemani mfalme wa Israeli alikuwa amevifanya katika hekalu la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyokuwa amesema.
sw.B: Akachukua kutoka huko hazina zote za nyumba ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na za ikulu, akavikatakata vyombo vyote vya dhahabu ambavyo Sulemani mfalme wa Israeli alikuwa amevifanya kwa ajili ya hekalu la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyokuwa amesema.
sw.R: Nebukadneza alichukua hazina zote za hekalu la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na za jumba la mfalme. Akavikata vipande vipande vyombo vyote vya dhahabu ambavyo Sulemani mfalme wa Israeli alikuwa amevitengeneza kwa ajili ya hekalu. Hivyo ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyokuwa amesema itakavyotokea.

vi.L: Vua ấy đem ra khỏi đó mọi báu vật của nhà {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} và báu vật của cung vua, và chặt vụn mọi khí cụ bằng vàng mà Sa-lô-môn vua Y-sơ-ra-ên đã làm trong đền thờ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, như {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã phán.
vi.B: Vua ấy lấy đi khỏi đó mọi báu vật của nhà {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} và của hoàng cung, và chặt vụn mọi khí cụ bằng vàng mà Sa-lô-môn vua Y-sơ-ra-ên đã làm cho đền thờ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, đúng như {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã phán.
vi.R: Nê-bu-cát-nết-sa lấy đi mọi báu vật trong đền thờ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} và trong hoàng cung. Vua ấy chặt vụn mọi đồ vật bằng vàng mà Sa-lô-môn vua Y-sơ-ra-ên đã làm cho đền thờ. Việc này xảy ra đúng như {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã báo trước.

ko.L: 그리고 그가 거기에서 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 집의 모든 보물과 왕의 집의 보물을 가져가고, 이스라엘 왕 솔로몬이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 성전에 만들어 둔 모든 금 그릇을 잘랐다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 말씀하신 대로였다.
ko.B: 그는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 집의 모든 보물과 왕궁의 보물을 거기에서 가져갔다. 그는 이스라엘 왕 솔로몬이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 성전을 위해 만든 금 그릇들을 모두 깨뜨렸다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 말씀하신 그대로였다.
ko.R: 느부갓네살은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 성전과 왕궁에서 보물을 모두 가져갔다. 그는 이스라엘 왕 솔로몬이 성전을 위해 만든 금 그릇들을 모두 조각냈다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 일어날 것이라고 말씀하신 그대로였다.

pt.L: E tirou dali todos os tesouros da casa {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} e os tesouros da casa do rei, e cortou em pedaços todos os utensílios de ouro que Salomão, rei de Israel, tinha feito no templo {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, como {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} tinha falado.
pt.B: Ele levou dali todos os tesouros da casa {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} e os do palácio real, e cortou em pedaços todos os utensílios de ouro que Salomão, rei de Israel, tinha feito para o templo {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, exatamente como {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} tinha dito.
pt.R: Nabucodonosor levou todos os tesouros do templo {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} e do palácio do rei. Ele cortou em pedaços todos os objetos de ouro que Salomão, rei de Israel, tinha feito para o templo. Foi exatamente o que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} tinha dito que ia acontecer.

am.L: ከዚያም {{divine_name:የእግዚአብሔር|የያህዌ}} ቤት መዝገብ ሁሉ፣ የንጉሡንም ቤት መዝገብ አወጣ፤ የእስራኤልም ንጉሥ ሰሎሞን {{divine_name:በእግዚአብሔር|በያህዌ}} መቅደስ የሠራቸውን የወርቅ ዕቃዎች ሁሉ {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} እንደ ተናገረ ቆራረጠ።
am.B: ከዚያም {{divine_name:የእግዚአብሔር|የያህዌ}} ቤተ መቅደስና የቤተ መንግሥቱን ሀብት ሁሉ ወሰደ፤ የእስራኤል ንጉሥ ሰሎሞን {{divine_name:ለእግዚአብሔር|ለያህዌ}} ቤተ መቅደስ የሠራቸውን የወርቅ ዕቃዎች ሁሉ {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} እንደ ተናገረው ቆራረጣቸው።
am.R: ናቡከደነፆር {{divine_name:ከእግዚአብሔር|ከያህዌ}} ቤተ መቅደስና ከቤተ መንግሥቱ ሀብቱን ሁሉ ወሰደ። የእስራኤል ንጉሥ ሰሎሞን ለቤተ መቅደሱ የሠራቸውን የወርቅ ዕቃዎች ሁሉ ቆራረጣቸው። ይህም {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} እንደሚሆን የተናገረው ነበር።

hi.L: और वह वहाँ से {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} के भवन के सब ख़ज़ाने और राजा के भवन के ख़ज़ाने निकाल ले गया, और उसने सोने के वे सब पात्र काट डाले जो इस्राएल के राजा सुलैमान ने {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} के मंदिर में बनाए थे, जैसा {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} ने कहा था।
hi.B: वह वहाँ से {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} के भवन के सब ख़ज़ाने और राजमहल के ख़ज़ाने उठा ले गया, और उसने सोने के वे सब पात्र काटकर टुकड़े-टुकड़े कर दिए जो इस्राएल के राजा सुलैमान ने {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} के मंदिर के लिए बनाए थे, ठीक जैसा {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} ने कहा था।
hi.R: नबूकदनेस्सर {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} के मंदिर और राजमहल के सारे ख़ज़ाने ले गया। उसने सोने की वे सब वस्तुएँ काटकर टुकड़े-टुकड़े कर दीं जो इस्राएल के राजा सुलैमान ने मंदिर के लिए बनाई थीं। यह ठीक वैसा ही हुआ जैसा {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} ने कहा था कि होगा।

ru.L: И вынес он оттуда все сокровища дома {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Яхве}} и сокровища дома царя, и изрубил все золотые сосуды, которые сделал Соломон, царь Израиля, в храме {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Яхве}}, как сказал {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}}.
ru.B: Он вывез оттуда все сокровища дома {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Яхве}} и сокровища царского дворца и изрубил все золотые сосуды, которые Соломон, царь Израиля, сделал для храма {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Яхве}}, как и говорил {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}}.
ru.R: Навуходоносор забрал все сокровища из храма {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Яхве}} и из царского дворца. Он разбил на куски все золотые вещи, которые Соломон, царь Израиля, сделал для храма. Так случилось то, о чём говорил {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}}.

ja.L: そして彼は、そこから{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}の家のすべての宝物と、王の家の宝物を運び出した。また、イスラエルの王ソロモンが{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}の神殿の中に作ったすべての金の器を切り刻んだ。{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}が語られたとおりであった。
ja.B: 彼はそこから、{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}の家の宝物と王宮の宝物をすべて運び去った。また、イスラエルの王ソロモンが{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}の神殿のために作った金の器を、すべて切り刻んだ。{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}が告げておられたとおりであった。
ja.R: ネブカドネツァルは、{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}の神殿と王宮から、宝物をすべて持ち去りました。また、イスラエルの王ソロモンが神殿のために作った金の器を、すべて切り刻みました。これは、{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}が前から、そうなると言っておられたとおりのことでした。

uk.L: І виніс він звідти всі скарби дому {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Ягве}} і скарби царського дому, і порубав усі золоті речі, які зробив Соломон, цар Ізраїлю, у храмі {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Ягве}}, як сказав {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Ягве}}.
uk.B: Він виніс звідти всі скарби дому {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Ягве}} і скарби царського палацу і порубав усі золоті речі, які Соломон, цар Ізраїлю, зробив для храму {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Ягве}}, як і сказав {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Ягве}}.
uk.R: Навуходоносор забрав усі скарби з храму {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Ягве}} і з царського палацу. Він порубав на шматки всі золоті речі, які Соломон, цар Ізраїлю, зробив для храму. Сталося саме те, що {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Ягве}} передрік.

decisions.choice: as Yahweh had spoken: through Isaiah to Hezekiah
decisions.reason: Isaiah had told Hezekiah that everything in his palace and all his ancestors had stored up would be carried off to Babylon (20:17). Temple treasure had been handed over before to buy off enemies (12:19; 18:15-16) and seized in war (14:14), but now Babylon took it all.

decisions.choice: cut up: broke the gold vessels into pieces or stripped off their gold
decisions.reason: The verb means to cut off or cut into pieces. It was used when Hezekiah stripped the gold from the temple doors (18:16). The gold was taken as metal, not kept as vessels. Some of Solomon's bronze furnishings were left until the city's fall (25:13-17).

decisions.choice: the vessels of gold that Solomon had made
decisions.reason: Solomon's gold furnishings for the temple are listed in 1 Kings 7:48-51.

decisions.choice: Nebuchadnezzar
decisions.reason: Readable names the king for "he", and leaves out the second "of the LORD" after "temple", which is clear from the first.

decisions.choice: cortou em pedaços; utensílios (L, B), objetos (R)
decisions.reason: "Cortar em pedaços" says that the gold was taken as metal (m2); the vessels are "utensílios" at Literal and Balanced, as 1 Kings 7:45-48 has them in Portuguese, and "objetos" at Readable.

decisions.choice: qitstsets "切り刻んだ"
decisions.reason: The verb means to cut off or cut up; the plain sense is kept and the meaning note can mention stripping the gold.

decisions.choice: "ネブカドネツァルは" (R)
decisions.reason: As the English Readable, the subject is named.

source.text: וְהִגְלָ֣ה אֶת־כָּל־יְ֠רוּשָׁלִַם וְֽאֶת־כָּל־הַשָּׂרִ֞ים וְאֵ֣ת׀כָּל־גִּבּוֹרֵ֣י הַחַ֗יִל עֲשֶׂ֤רֶת אֲלָפִים֙ גּוֹלֶ֔ה וְכָל־הֶחָרָ֖שׁ וְהַמַּסְגֵּ֑ר לֹ֣א נִשְׁאַ֔ר זוּלַ֖ת דַּלַּ֥ת עַם־הָאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he exiled all Jerusalem and all the princes and all [the] mighty [men] of the valor, ten thousand exiles, and every craftsman and the smith; not was left except [the] poorest of [the] people of the land.

en.L: And he exiled all Jerusalem and all the princes and all the mighty men of valor, 10,000 exiles, and every craftsman and smith; none was left except the poorest of the people of the land.
en.B: He carried all Jerusalem into exile: all the officials and all the mighty warriors, 10,000 captives, and all the craftsmen and smiths. No one was left except the poorest people of the land.
en.R: He took the people of Jerusalem away as captives. He took all the leaders and all the best soldiers, 10,000 people in all, and all the skilled workers and metalworkers. Only the poorest people in the land were left.

es.L: Y llevó cautiva a toda Jerusalén, y a todos los príncipes y a todos los valientes guerreros, 10 000 cautivos, y a todos los artesanos y herreros; no quedó nadie excepto los más pobres del pueblo de la tierra.
es.B: Llevó al destierro a toda Jerusalén: a todos los funcionarios y a todos los guerreros valientes, 10 000 cautivos, y a todos los artesanos y herreros. No quedó nadie sino la gente más pobre del país.
es.R: Se llevó como prisioneros a la gente de Jerusalén. Se llevó a todos los jefes y a los mejores soldados, 10 000 personas en total, y a todos los artesanos y los que trabajaban el metal. Solo quedó la gente más pobre del país.

fr.L: Et il déporta tout Jérusalem, tous les princes et tous les vaillants guerriers, dix mille déportés, et tous les artisans et les forgerons ; il ne resta que les plus pauvres du peuple du pays.
fr.B: Il emmena en exil tout Jérusalem : tous les chefs et tous les vaillants guerriers, dix mille captifs, ainsi que tous les artisans et les forgerons. Il ne resta que la population la plus pauvre du pays.
fr.R: Il a emmené les gens de Jérusalem comme prisonniers. Il a emmené tous les chefs et tous les meilleurs soldats, dix mille personnes en tout, et tous les artisans et ceux qui travaillaient les métaux. Il n’est resté que les gens les plus pauvres du pays.

sw.L: Naye akawahamisha Yerusalemu wote, na wakuu wote na mashujaa wote wa vita, mateka 10,000, na kila fundi na mhunzi; hakubaki mtu ila maskini kabisa wa watu wa nchi.
sw.B: Aliwachukua uhamishoni Yerusalemu wote: maafisa wote na mashujaa wote wa vita, mateka 10,000, na mafundi wote na wahunzi. Hakubaki mtu ila watu maskini kabisa wa nchi.
sw.R: Aliwachukua mateka watu wa Yerusalemu. Aliwachukua viongozi wote na askari wote hodari, watu 10,000 kwa jumla, na mafundi wote stadi na wahunzi. Ni watu maskini kabisa wa nchi tu waliobaki.

vi.L: Vua ấy bắt cả Giê-ru-sa-lem lưu đày, mọi thủ lĩnh và mọi dũng sĩ, mười nghìn người lưu đày, cùng mọi thợ thủ công và thợ rèn; không còn ai sót lại ngoài những người nghèo nhất trong dân của xứ.
vi.B: Vua ấy bắt cả Giê-ru-sa-lem đi lưu đày: mọi quan chức và mọi chiến sĩ dũng mãnh, mười nghìn người bị bắt, cùng mọi thợ thủ công và thợ rèn. Không còn ai ở lại ngoài những người nghèo nhất trong xứ.
vi.R: Vua ấy bắt dân Giê-ru-sa-lem đi làm tù binh. Vua bắt mọi thủ lĩnh và mọi binh sĩ giỏi nhất, tổng cộng mười nghìn người, cùng mọi thợ lành nghề và thợ kim loại. Chỉ còn những người nghèo nhất trong xứ ở lại.

ko.L: 그리고 그가 온 예루살렘과 모든 고관과 모든 용사, 곧 포로 만 명과 모든 장인과 대장장이를 사로잡아 갔다. 그 땅 백성 가운데 가장 가난한 자들 외에는 남은 자가 없었다.
ko.B: 그는 예루살렘의 모든 사람, 곧 모든 고관과 모든 용사를 사로잡아 갔는데, 포로가 만 명이었다. 모든 장인과 대장장이도 끌려갔다. 그 땅에서 가장 가난한 백성 외에는 아무도 남지 않았다.
ko.R: 그는 예루살렘 사람들을 포로로 잡아갔다. 모든 지도자와 가장 뛰어난 군인들, 모두 만 명을 데려갔다. 기술자들과 쇠붙이를 다루는 사람들도 모두 데려갔다. 그 땅에는 가장 가난한 사람들만 남았다.

pt.L: E levou para o exílio toda Jerusalém, e todos os príncipes, e todos os guerreiros valentes, dez mil exilados, e todo artífice e ferreiro; ninguém ficou, a não ser os mais pobres do povo da terra.
pt.B: Ele levou para o exílio toda Jerusalém: todos os oficiais e todos os guerreiros valentes, dez mil prisioneiros, e todos os artífices e ferreiros. Ninguém ficou, a não ser os mais pobres do povo da terra.
pt.R: Ele levou o povo de Jerusalém como prisioneiro. Levou todos os líderes e todos os melhores soldados, dez mil pessoas ao todo, e todos os artesãos e ferreiros. Só os mais pobres da terra ficaram.

am.L: ኢየሩሳሌምንም ሁሉ፣ አለቆቹንም ሁሉ፣ ጽኑዓን ኃያላኑንም ሁሉ፣ 10,000 ምርኮኞችን፣ የእጅ ጥበብ ባለሙያውንም ሁሉ፣ ብረት ሠሪውንም አፈለሰ፤ ከአገሩ ሕዝብ ከድሆቹ በቀር ማንም አልቀረም።
am.B: ኢየሩሳሌምን ሁሉ ማርኮ ወሰደ፤ መኳንንቱን ሁሉ፣ ጀግኖቹን ተዋጊዎች ሁሉ፣ 10,000 ምርኮኞችን፣ የእጅ ጥበብ ባለሙያዎችንና ብረት ሠሪዎችን ሁሉ ወሰደ። ከአገሩ ሕዝብ በጣም ድሆች ከሆኑት በቀር ማንም አልቀረም።
am.R: የኢየሩሳሌምን ሕዝብ ማርኮ ወሰደ። መሪዎቹን ሁሉና ምርጥ ወታደሮቹን ሁሉ፣ በአጠቃላይ 10,000 ሰዎችን ወሰደ። የእጅ ሙያተኞችንና ብረት ሠሪዎችን ሁሉ ደግሞ ወሰደ። በአገሩ የቀሩት በጣም ድሆች የሆኑት ሰዎች ብቻ ነበሩ።

hi.L: और उसने सारे यरूशलेम को, और सब हाकिमों को और सब पराक्रमी वीर योद्धाओं को, 10,000 निर्वासितों को, और सब कारीगरों और लोहारों को निर्वासित कर दिया; देश के लोगों में से सबसे कंगालों को छोड़ कोई न बचा।
hi.B: वह सारे यरूशलेम को निर्वासन में ले गया: सब हाकिमों और सब वीर योद्धाओं को, 10,000 बंदियों को, और सब कारीगरों और लोहारों को। देश के सबसे कंगाल लोगों को छोड़ कोई न बचा।
hi.R: वह यरूशलेम के लोगों को बंदी बनाकर ले गया। वह सब अगुवों को और सब सबसे अच्छे सैनिकों को ले गया, कुल 10,000 लोगों को, और सब कुशल कारीगरों और धातु का काम करनेवालों को भी। देश में केवल सबसे कंगाल लोग ही बचे।

ru.L: И переселил он весь Иерусалим, и всех князей, и всех воинов-богатырей — 10 000 переселенцев, — и всех мастеров и кузнецов; не осталось никого, кроме бедноты народа земли.
ru.B: Он увёл в изгнание весь Иерусалим: всех вельмож и всех воинов-богатырей, 10 000 пленников, и всех мастеров и кузнецов. Не осталось никого, кроме самых бедных людей страны.
ru.R: Он угнал в плен жителей Иерусалима. Он угнал всех начальников и всех храбрых воинов, всего 10 000 человек, и всех мастеров и кузнецов. В стране остались только самые бедные люди.

ja.L: そして彼は、エルサレムのすべて、すべての高官たち、すべての力ある勇士たち、一万人の捕囚の民、またすべての職人と鍛冶屋を捕らえ移した。国の民の最も貧しい者のほかは、だれも残されなかった。
ja.B: 彼はエルサレムのすべての人々を捕囚として連れ去った。すべての高官たち、すべての勇士たち、合わせて一万人の捕囚の民と、すべての職人と鍛冶屋である。残されたのは、国の民の中で最も貧しい者たちだけであった。
ja.R: ネブカドネツァルは、エルサレムの人々を捕虜にして連れて行きました。指導者たちや優れた兵士たちをみな、全部で一万人を連れて行き、腕のいい職人や金属を扱う職人もみな連れて行きました。国に残されたのは、最も貧しい人々だけでした。

uk.L: І вигнав він увесь Єрусалим, і всіх князів, і всіх хоробрих воїнів, десять тисяч вигнанців, і кожного ремісника і коваля; не лишилося нікого, крім найбідніших із народу землі.
uk.B: Він вигнав у полон увесь Єрусалим: усіх вельмож і всіх хоробрих воїнів, десять тисяч полонених, і всіх ремісників та ковалів. Не лишилося нікого, крім найбідніших людей краю.
uk.R: Він забрав людей Єрусалима в полон. Він забрав усіх провідників і всіх найкращих воїнів, усього десять тисяч людей, і всіх умілих ремісників і ковалів. У краю лишилися тільки найбідніші люди.

decisions.choice: ten: the form read aloud
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) have a different form of the number ten; the scribes marked the usual form to be read aloud (qere). The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: all Jerusalem: the city's leading people, not every person
decisions.reason: The verse itself says the poorest were left, and Jerusalem still had a king and people under Zedekiah (verses 17-20; 25:11). "All Jerusalem" means the city as a community, and the lists that follow say who was taken.

decisions.choice: smith: a metalworker, though the exact trade is uncertain
decisions.reason: The word comes from a verb meaning "to shut" or "to close". It may name smiths, makers of locks and fittings, or men who built or held fortifications. Taking away the craftsmen left Judah unable to make weapons or repair its walls.

decisions.choice: ten thousand exiles: a total, probably counted with the groups of verse 16
decisions.reason: Verse 16 counts seven thousand fighting men and a thousand craftsmen. The ten thousand here may include them, together with the officials and the court, or the two verses may give two separate counts. Jeremiah 52:28 gives 3,023 people of Judah taken in Nebuchadnezzar's seventh year, perhaps counting only one group.

decisions.choice: the poorest of the people of the land
decisions.reason: Those left were the poor who had no land, rank or skill that mattered to Babylon. The same happened after the city's fall (25:12).

decisions.choice: officials, mighty warriors (Balanced); leaders, best soldiers (Readable)
decisions.reason: The princes are "officials" at Balanced and "leaders" at Readable, as in these books. "Mighty men of valor" are fighting men known for their strength and courage; Balanced says "mighty warriors" and Readable "best soldiers".

decisions.choice: dez mil (in words); ferreiro (every level); levou para o exílio (L, B)
decisions.reason: Round numbers are written in words, as the book does (3:4), where the English writes "10,000". The uncertain trade (m3) is "ferreiro", the plain word for a smith, at every level; Readable keeps it too, where the English says "metalworkers", since it is already plain Portuguese. The exile keeps the wording 17:6 sets for the book.

decisions.choice: to exile (galah, hiphil) is "አፈለሰ" (Literal), "ማርኮ ወሰደ" (Balanced, Readable); the exiles "ምርኮኞች".
decisions.reason: As the Amharic 2 Kings 17:6 for the exile of Israel, so that the two exiles read alike; the terms list gives "ግዞት, ምርኮ" for exile.

decisions.choice: निर्वासित करना, निर्वासन (L, B); बंदी बनाकर ले जाना (R)
decisions.reason: The exile to Babylon is निर्वासन, the word of Matthew 1:11-12 and 1:17 (बाबुल का निर्वासन), so the reader of Matthew hears the same event; Readable says plainly that the people were taken away as captives, as Matthew 1:12 does at Readable. The mighty men are वीर योद्धा, as the history-books note.

decisions.choice: "переселил", "переселенцы" (L); "увёл в изгнание", "пленники" (B); "угнал в плен" (R)
decisions.reason: Each level uses the words its own Matthew 1:11-12 uses for the exile to Babylon in this translation ("переселение" at Literal, "изгнание" at Balanced, "угнали" at Readable), so the reader of the genealogy and of this chapter meets the same event in the same words.

decisions.choice: "воины-богатыри" (L, B); "храбрые воины" (R)
decisions.reason: The history note's wording for gibborim.

decisions.choice: galah "捕らえ移した" (L), "捕囚として連れ去った" (B), "捕虜にして連れて行きました" (R), as 2KI 17:6
decisions.reason: The Kings forms for exile.

decisions.choice: charash "職人", masger "鍛冶屋" (L, B); "腕のいい職人や金属を扱う職人" (R)
decisions.reason: The trade of the masger is uncertain; the English says smiths, metalworkers, and 鍛冶屋 is the plain word for that.

source.text: וַיֶּ֥גֶל אֶת־יְהוֹיָכִ֖ין בָּבֶ֑לָה וְאֶת־אֵ֣ם הַ֠מֶּלֶךְ וְאֶת־נְשֵׁ֨י הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ וְאֶת־סָרִיסָ֗יו וְאֵת֙ אֵילֵ֣י הָאָ֔רֶץ הוֹלִ֛יךְ גּוֹלָ֥ה מִירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם בָּבֶֽלָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And he exiled Jehoiachin to Babylon, and [the] mother of the king and [the] wives of the king and his eunuchs and [the] leaders of the land he led [into] exile from Jerusalem to Babylon.

en.L: And he exiled Jehoiachin to Babylon; and the mother of the king and the wives of the king and his eunuchs and the leading men of the land he led away [into] exile from Jerusalem to Babylon.
en.B: He carried Jehoiachin into exile to Babylon. The king's mother, the king's wives, his court officers and the leading men of the land he also took into exile from Jerusalem to Babylon.
en.R: Nebuchadnezzar took Jehoiachin to Babylon as a captive. He also took the king's mother, his wives, his palace officials and the most important men of the land. He carried them all away from Jerusalem to Babylon.

es.L: Y llevó cautivo a Joaquín a Babilonia; y a la madre del rey, y a las mujeres del rey, y a sus eunucos y a los poderosos de la tierra los llevó cautivos de Jerusalén a Babilonia.
es.B: Llevó a Joaquín al destierro en Babilonia. También llevó al destierro, de Jerusalén a Babilonia, a la madre del rey, a las esposas del rey, a los oficiales de su corte y a los hombres principales del país.
es.R: Nabucodonosor se llevó a Joaquín a Babilonia como prisionero. También se llevó a la madre del rey, a sus esposas, a los funcionarios de su palacio y a los hombres más importantes del país. Se los llevó a todos de Jerusalén a Babilonia.

fr.L: Et il déporta Joïakin à Babylone ; et la mère du roi, les femmes du roi, ses eunuques et les notables du pays, il les emmena en exil de Jérusalem à Babylone.
fr.B: Il emmena Joïakin en exil à Babylone. La mère du roi, les femmes du roi, ses hauts fonctionnaires et les notables du pays, il les emmena aussi en exil de Jérusalem à Babylone.
fr.R: Nabuchodonosor a emmené Joïakin à Babylone comme prisonnier. Il a aussi emmené la mère du roi, ses femmes, les fonctionnaires du palais et les hommes les plus importants du pays. Il les a tous emmenés de Jérusalem à Babylone.

sw.L: Naye akamhamisha Yehoyakini mpaka Babeli; na mama wa mfalme na wake za mfalme na matowashi wake na wakuu wa nchi akawapeleka uhamishoni kutoka Yerusalemu mpaka Babeli.
sw.B: Alimchukua Yehoyakini uhamishoni mpaka Babeli. Mama wa mfalme, wake za mfalme, wakuu wa ikulu yake na watu mashuhuri wa nchi pia aliwachukua uhamishoni kutoka Yerusalemu mpaka Babeli.
sw.R: Nebukadneza alimchukua Yehoyakini mpaka Babeli akiwa mateka. Aliwachukua pia mama wa mfalme, wake zake, maafisa wa jumba lake na watu muhimu kabisa wa nchi. Aliwachukua wote kutoka Yerusalemu mpaka Babeli.

vi.L: Vua ấy bắt Giê-hô-gia-kin lưu đày sang Ba-by-lôn; mẹ vua, các vợ vua, các hoạn quan của vua và những người quyền thế trong xứ, vua ấy dẫn đi lưu đày từ Giê-ru-sa-lem sang Ba-by-lôn.
vi.B: Vua ấy bắt Giê-hô-gia-kin lưu đày sang Ba-by-lôn. Mẹ vua, các vợ vua, các triều thần và những người quyền thế trong xứ cũng bị vua ấy bắt đi lưu đày từ Giê-ru-sa-lem sang Ba-by-lôn.
vi.R: Nê-bu-cát-nết-sa bắt Giê-hô-gia-kin đem sang Ba-by-lôn làm tù binh. Vua ấy cũng bắt mẹ vua, các vợ vua, các quan chức trong cung và những người quan trọng nhất trong xứ. Vua ấy đem tất cả họ từ Giê-ru-sa-lem sang Ba-by-lôn.

ko.L: 그리고 그가 여호야긴을 바빌론으로 사로잡아 갔다. 그리고 왕의 어머니와 왕의 아내들과 그의 내시들과 그 땅의 유력자들을 예루살렘에서 바빌론으로 포로로 끌고 갔다.
ko.B: 그는 여호야긴을 바빌론으로 사로잡아 갔다. 왕의 어머니와 왕의 아내들과 그의 관리들과 그 땅의 유력자들도 예루살렘에서 바빌론으로 포로로 끌고 갔다.
ko.R: 느부갓네살은 여호야긴을 포로로 잡아 바빌론으로 데려갔다. 그는 왕의 어머니와 왕의 아내들과 왕궁 관리들과 그 땅의 가장 중요한 사람들도 데려갔다. 그는 그들을 모두 예루살렘에서 바빌론으로 끌고 갔다.

pt.L: E levou Joaquim para o exílio na Babilônia; e a mãe do rei, e as mulheres do rei, e os seus eunucos, e os poderosos da terra, ele os levou para o exílio, de Jerusalém para a Babilônia.
pt.B: Ele levou Joaquim para o exílio na Babilônia. Levou também para o exílio, de Jerusalém para a Babilônia, a mãe do rei, as mulheres do rei, os funcionários da corte e os homens importantes da terra.
pt.R: Nabucodonosor levou Joaquim prisioneiro para a Babilônia. Levou também a mãe do rei, as mulheres dele, os oficiais do palácio e os homens mais importantes da terra. Levou todos eles de Jerusalém para a Babilônia.

am.L: ዮአኪንንም ወደ ባቢሎን አፈለሰ፤ የንጉሡንም እናት፣ የንጉሡንም ሚስቶች፣ ጃንደረቦቹንም፣ የአገሩንም ታላላቆች ከኢየሩሳሌም ወደ ባቢሎን በምርኮ ወሰዳቸው።
am.B: ዮአኪንን ማርኮ ወደ ባቢሎን ወሰደው። የንጉሡን እናት፣ የንጉሡን ሚስቶች፣ የቤተ መንግሥቱን ሹማምንትና የአገሩን ታላላቅ ሰዎች ደግሞ ከኢየሩሳሌም ወደ ባቢሎን ማርኮ ወሰዳቸው።
am.R: ናቡከደነፆር ዮአኪንን ማርኮ ወደ ባቢሎን ወሰደው። የንጉሡን እናት፣ ሚስቶቹን፣ የቤተ መንግሥቱን ሹማምንትና የአገሩን ታላላቅ ሰዎች ደግሞ ወሰደ። ሁሉንም ከኢየሩሳሌም ወደ ባቢሎን አጋዛቸው።

hi.L: और वह यहोयाकीन को निर्वासित करके बाबुल ले गया; और राजा की माता और राजा की पत्नियों और उसके खोजों और देश के प्रमुख पुरुषों को वह यरूशलेम से बाबुल को निर्वासन [में] ले गया।
hi.B: वह यहोयाकीन को निर्वासन में बाबुल ले गया। राजा की माता, राजा की पत्नियों, उसके दरबारियों और देश के प्रमुख पुरुषों को भी वह यरूशलेम से निर्वासन में बाबुल ले गया।
hi.R: नबूकदनेस्सर यहोयाकीन को बंदी बनाकर बाबुल ले गया। वह राजा की माता को, उसकी पत्नियों को, उसके महल के कर्मचारियों को और देश के सबसे बड़े लोगों को भी ले गया। वह उन सब को यरूशलेम से बाबुल ले गया।

ru.L: И переселил он Иехонию в Вавилон; и мать царя, и жён царя, и его евнухов, и знатных людей земли он увёл переселенцами из Иерусалима в Вавилон.
ru.B: Он увёл Иехонию в изгнание в Вавилон. Мать царя, жён царя, его придворных и знатных людей страны он тоже увёл в изгнание из Иерусалима в Вавилон.
ru.R: Навуходоносор угнал Иехонию в Вавилон как пленника. Он угнал и мать царя, и его жён, и придворных, и самых важных людей страны. Он увёл их всех из Иерусалима в Вавилон.

ja.L: そして彼はヨヤキンをバビロンへ捕らえ移した。また王の母と、王の妻たちと、彼の宦官たちと、国の有力者たちを、捕囚としてエルサレムからバビロンへ連れて行った。
ja.B: 彼はヨヤキンを捕囚としてバビロンへ連れ去った。王の母、王の妻たち、宮廷の役人たち、そして国の有力者たちも、捕囚としてエルサレムからバビロンへ連れ去った。
ja.R: ネブカドネツァルは、ヨヤキンを捕虜にしてバビロンへ連れて行きました。王の母や王の妻たち、王宮の役人たち、そして国の重要な人々も連れて行きました。この人々をみな、エルサレムからバビロンへ連れて行ったのです。

uk.L: І вигнав він Єгояхина до Вавилону; і матір царя, і жінок царя, і його євнухів, і можних землі повів він [у] вигнання з Єрусалима до Вавилону.
uk.B: Він вигнав Єгояхина до Вавилону. Матір царя, жінок царя, його придворних і знатних людей краю він також повів у полон з Єрусалима до Вавилону.
uk.R: Навуходоносор забрав Єгояхина до Вавилону як полоненого. Він також забрав матір царя, його жінок, його палацових урядовців і найважливіших людей краю. Він повів їх усіх з Єрусалима до Вавилону.

decisions.choice: the leading men: the form read aloud
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) spell the word differently; the scribes marked this form to be read aloud (qere). Both name the powerful men of the land.

decisions.choice: the leading men of the land: its powerful and wealthy men
decisions.reason: The word can mean rams, the strong leaders of a flock, and is used of chiefs and nobles (Exodus 15:15; Ezekiel 17:13). With the court, they made up Judah's ruling class.

decisions.choice: he exiled Jehoiachin to Babylon
decisions.reason: Jeremiah had said that Coniah (Jehoiachin) and his mother would be thrown into a land where they were not born (Jeremiah 22:24-27). His letter to the exiles names this same group: the king, the queen mother, the court officials and the princes (Jeremiah 29:2). Ezekiel was among those taken, and dated his book by this exile (Ezekiel 1:2).

decisions.choice: court officers (Balanced); palace officials (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 12. Readable says "most important men" for the leading men of the land and names Nebuchadnezzar for "he".

decisions.choice: sarisim: "ጃንደረቦች" (Literal), "የቤተ መንግሥቱ ሹማምንት" (Balanced, Readable).
decisions.reason: As at 23:11: Literal keeps the traditional court title, the other levels say what they were.

decisions.choice: saris "宦官たち" (L), "宮廷の役人たち" (B), "王宮の役人たち" (R); 'ele ha'arets "国の有力者たち" (L, B), "国の重要な人々" (R)
decisions.reason: The leading men are the land's powerful and wealthy; saris as 24:12.

source.text: וְאֵת֩ כָּל־אַנְשֵׁ֨י הַחַ֜יִל שִׁבְעַ֣ת אֲלָפִ֗ים וְהֶחָרָ֤שׁ וְהַמַּסְגֵּר֙ אֶ֔לֶף הַכֹּ֕ל גִּבּוֹרִ֖ים עֹשֵׂ֣י מִלְחָמָ֑ה וַיְבִיאֵ֧ם מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֛ל גּוֹלָ֖ה בָּבֶֽלָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And all [the] men of the valor, seven thousand, and the craftsman and the smith, a thousand, the all [were] mighty, makers of war, and brought them [the] king of Babylon [as] exiles to Babylon.

en.L: And all the men of valor, 7,000, and the craftsmen and the smiths, a thousand, all [of them] mighty, makers of war, the king of Babylon brought them [as] exiles to Babylon.
en.B: The king of Babylon brought to Babylon as exiles all the men of valor, 7,000, and the craftsmen and smiths, a thousand, all of them strong men fit for war.
en.R: The king of Babylon also took to Babylon as captives 7,000 of the best fighting men and a thousand skilled workers and metalworkers. All of them were strong and able to fight.

es.L: Y a todos los hombres valientes, 7 000, y a los artesanos y herreros, mil, todos ellos fuertes y aptos para la guerra, el rey de Babilonia los llevó cautivos a Babilonia.
es.B: El rey de Babilonia llevó cautivos a Babilonia a todos los hombres valientes, 7 000, y a los artesanos y herreros, mil, todos ellos hombres fuertes y aptos para la guerra.
es.R: El rey de Babilonia también se llevó como prisioneros a Babilonia a 7 000 de los mejores soldados y a 1 000 artesanos y trabajadores del metal. Todos eran fuertes y capaces de pelear.

fr.L: Et tous les hommes vaillants, sept mille, et les artisans et les forgerons, mille, tous [étaient] des hommes forts, faisant la guerre ; le roi de Babylone les emmena [comme] déportés à Babylone.
fr.B: Le roi de Babylone emmena en exil à Babylone tous les hommes vaillants, sept mille, ainsi que les artisans et les forgerons, mille, tous des hommes robustes et aptes à la guerre.
fr.R: Le roi de Babylone a aussi emmené à Babylone comme prisonniers sept mille des meilleurs combattants et mille artisans et ouvriers des métaux. Tous étaient forts et capables de combattre.

sw.L: Na mashujaa wote, 7,000, na mafundi na wahunzi, elfu moja, wote [walikuwa] hodari, watu wa vita, mfalme wa Babeli akawaleta [wakiwa] mateka mpaka Babeli.
sw.B: Mfalme wa Babeli aliwaleta Babeli kama mateka mashujaa wote, 7,000, na mafundi na wahunzi, elfu moja, wote wakiwa watu wenye nguvu wanaofaa kwa vita.
sw.R: Mfalme wa Babeli aliwachukua pia mpaka Babeli kama mateka askari hodari 7,000, na mafundi stadi na wahunzi elfu moja. Wote walikuwa na nguvu na waliweza kupigana vita.

vi.L: Mọi dũng sĩ, bảy nghìn người, cùng thợ thủ công và thợ rèn, một nghìn người, tất cả [đều là] người mạnh mẽ, giỏi chiến trận, vua Ba-by-lôn đem họ đi lưu đày sang Ba-by-lôn.
vi.B: Vua Ba-by-lôn đem sang Ba-by-lôn làm người lưu đày mọi dũng sĩ, bảy nghìn người, cùng thợ thủ công và thợ rèn, một nghìn người, tất cả đều là người mạnh mẽ, có thể ra trận.
vi.R: Vua Ba-by-lôn cũng bắt sang Ba-by-lôn bảy nghìn binh sĩ giỏi nhất và một nghìn thợ lành nghề và thợ kim loại. Tất cả đều khỏe mạnh và có thể ra trận.

ko.L: 그리고 모든 용사 칠천 명과 장인과 대장장이 천 명, 모두 힘센 전사들을 바빌론 왕이 바빌론으로 포로로 끌고 갔다.
ko.B: 바빌론 왕은 용사 칠천 명과 장인과 대장장이 천 명을 포로로 바빌론에 끌고 갔다. 그들은 모두 싸움에 능한 힘센 사람들이었다.
ko.R: 바빌론 왕은 가장 뛰어난 군인 칠천 명과 기술자와 쇠붙이를 다루는 사람 천 명도 포로로 바빌론에 데려갔다. 그들은 모두 힘이 세고 싸울 수 있는 사람들이었다.

pt.L: E todos os homens de valor, sete mil, e os artífices e os ferreiros, mil, todos [eles] fortes, aptos para a guerra, o rei da Babilônia os levou [como] exilados para a Babilônia.
pt.B: O rei da Babilônia levou para a Babilônia como exilados todos os homens de valor, sete mil, e os artífices e ferreiros, mil, todos eles homens fortes e aptos para a guerra.
pt.R: O rei da Babilônia também levou para a Babilônia como prisioneiros sete mil dos melhores soldados e mil artesãos e ferreiros. Todos eram fortes e capazes de lutar.

am.L: ጽኑዓን ሰዎችንም ሁሉ፣ 7,000፣ የእጅ ጥበብ ባለሙያዎችንና ብረት ሠሪዎችን አንድ ሺህ፣ ሁሉንም ለጦርነት የሚሆኑ ኃያላን የባቢሎን ንጉሥ ምርኮኞች አድርጎ ወደ ባቢሎን አመጣቸው።
am.B: የባቢሎን ንጉሥ ጽኑዓን ሰዎችን ሁሉ፣ 7,000፣ የእጅ ጥበብ ባለሙያዎችንና ብረት ሠሪዎችን አንድ ሺህ፣ ሁሉንም ለጦርነት ብቁ የሆኑ ብርቱዎች ማርኮ ወደ ባቢሎን አመጣቸው።
am.R: የባቢሎን ንጉሥ 7,000 ምርጥ ተዋጊዎችንና አንድ ሺህ የእጅ ሙያተኞችንና ብረት ሠሪዎችን ደግሞ ማርኮ ወደ ባቢሎን ወሰዳቸው። ሁሉም ብርቱዎችና ለመዋጋት ብቁ ነበሩ።

hi.L: और सब वीर पुरुष, 7,000, और कारीगर और लोहार, एक हज़ार, सब [के सब] बलवान, युद्ध करनेवाले, उन्हें बाबुल का राजा निर्वासित [करके] बाबुल ले आया।
hi.B: बाबुल का राजा सब वीर पुरुषों को, 7,000, और कारीगरों और लोहारों को, एक हज़ार, निर्वासित करके बाबुल ले आया; वे सब बलवान और युद्ध के योग्य पुरुष थे।
hi.R: बाबुल का राजा 7,000 सबसे अच्छे योद्धाओं को और एक हज़ार कुशल कारीगरों और धातु का काम करनेवालों को भी बंदी बनाकर बाबुल ले गया। वे सब बलवान थे और लड़ने के योग्य थे।

ru.L: И всех доблестных мужей, 7000, и мастеров и кузнецов — тысячу, всех сильных, способных к войне, — их привёл царь Вавилона переселенцами в Вавилон.
ru.B: Царь Вавилона увёл в изгнание в Вавилон всех доблестных воинов, 7000, и мастеров и кузнецов, тысячу; все они были сильными и годными к войне.
ru.R: Царь Вавилона угнал в Вавилон ещё 7000 лучших воинов и тысячу мастеров и кузнецов. Все они были сильными и умели воевать.

ja.L: また、すべての勇士たち七千人と、職人と鍛冶屋千人、皆、戦いをする力ある者たちを、バビロンの王は捕囚としてバビロンへ連れて行った。
ja.B: バビロンの王は、すべての勇士たち七千人と、職人と鍛冶屋千人を、捕囚としてバビロンへ連れて行った。皆、戦いに適した屈強な者たちであった。
ja.R: バビロンの王は、優れた兵士七千人と、腕のいい職人や金属を扱う職人千人も、捕虜としてバビロンへ連れて行きました。みな力が強く、戦うことのできる人たちでした。

uk.L: І всіх хоробрих людей, сім тисяч, і ремісників і ковалів, тисячу, усіх сильних, здатних до війни, — їх привів цар Вавилону [як] вигнанців до Вавилону.
uk.B: Цар Вавилону привів до Вавилону як полонених усіх хоробрих людей, сім тисяч, і ремісників та ковалів, тисячу, усіх міцних чоловіків, здатних воювати.
uk.R: Цар Вавилону також забрав до Вавилону як полонених сім тисяч найкращих воїнів і тисячу вмілих ремісників і ковалів. Усі вони були сильні й здатні воювати.

decisions.choice: men of valor: able fighting men
decisions.reason: The word for valor also means strength, ability and wealth, and "men of valor" can mean men of standing. Next to "makers of war" it means men able to fight.

decisions.choice: all of them mighty, makers of war: said of the whole group
decisions.reason: The phrase may describe all eight thousand, or only the craftsmen, who were strong men who could also serve in war. Either way, Babylon took the men who could have defended or rebuilt Judah.

decisions.choice: seven thousand ... a thousand: counts within the exile of verse 14
decisions.reason: See verse 14 on how these numbers relate to the ten thousand there.

decisions.choice: the king of Babylon first
decisions.reason: The Hebrew lists the groups first and then says "the king of Babylon brought them". Balanced and Readable start with the king, as English does; Readable keeps "metalworkers" for the smiths as in verse 14.

decisions.choice: sete mil; mil (in words)
decisions.reason: Round numbers in words, as in verse 14, where the English writes "7,000".

decisions.choice: anshei hechayil "勇士たち" (L, B), "優れた兵士" (R); "戦いをする力ある者たち" (L), "戦いに適した屈強な者たち" (B), "力が強く、戦うことのできる人たち" (R)
decisions.reason: Able fighting men; the closing phrase describes the whole group.

source.text: וַיַּמְלֵ֧ךְ מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֛ל אֶת־מַתַּנְיָ֥ה דֹד֖וֹ תַּחְתָּ֑יו וַיַּסֵּ֥ב אֶת־שְׁמ֖וֹ צִדְקִיָּֽהוּ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And made king [the] king of Babylon Mattaniah his uncle in his place, and he changed his name [to] Zedekiah.

en.L: And the king of Babylon made Mattaniah his uncle king in his place, and he changed his name [to] Zedekiah.
en.B: The king of Babylon made Jehoiachin's uncle Mattaniah king in his place and changed his name to Zedekiah.
en.R: The king of Babylon made Jehoiachin's uncle Mattaniah king in his place. He changed Mattaniah's name to Zedekiah.

es.L: Y el rey de Babilonia puso por rey en su lugar a Matanías, tío de él, y le cambió el nombre [por] Sedequías.
es.B: El rey de Babilonia puso como rey en su lugar a Matanías, tío de Joaquín, y le cambió el nombre por el de Sedequías.
es.R: El rey de Babilonia hizo rey en lugar de Joaquín a su tío Matanías. Le cambió el nombre a Matanías y le puso Sedequías.

fr.L: Et le roi de Babylone fit roi Mattania, son oncle, à sa place, et il changea son nom [en] Sédécias.
fr.B: Le roi de Babylone établit roi à sa place Mattania, l’oncle de Joïakin, et il changea son nom en Sédécias.
fr.R: Le roi de Babylone a fait roi Mattania, l’oncle de Joïakin, à sa place. Il a changé le nom de Mattania en Sédécias.

sw.L: Naye mfalme wa Babeli akamtawaza Matania baba yake mdogo kuwa mfalme mahali pake, akabadilisha jina lake [kuwa] Sedekia.
sw.B: Mfalme wa Babeli alimtawaza Matania, baba mdogo wa Yehoyakini, kuwa mfalme mahali pake, akabadilisha jina lake kuwa Sedekia.
sw.R: Mfalme wa Babeli alimfanya Matania, baba mdogo wa Yehoyakini, kuwa mfalme mahali pake. Akabadilisha jina la Matania kuwa Sedekia.

vi.L: Vua Ba-by-lôn lập Mát-ta-nia, chú của ông, làm vua thay ông, và đổi tên ông [thành] Sê-đê-kia.
vi.B: Vua Ba-by-lôn lập Mát-ta-nia, chú của Giê-hô-gia-kin, làm vua thay ông, và đổi tên Mát-ta-nia thành Sê-đê-kia.
vi.R: Vua Ba-by-lôn lập Mát-ta-nia, chú của Giê-hô-gia-kin, làm vua thay ông. Vua ấy đổi tên Mát-ta-nia thành Sê-đê-kia.

ko.L: 그리고 바빌론 왕이 그의 삼촌 맛다니야를 그를 대신하여 왕으로 삼고, 그의 이름을 시드기야로 바꾸었다.
ko.B: 바빌론 왕은 여호야긴의 삼촌 맛다니야를 그 대신 왕으로 세우고, 그의 이름을 시드기야로 바꾸었다.
ko.R: 바빌론 왕은 여호야긴의 삼촌 맛다니야를 그 대신 왕으로 세웠다. 그는 맛다니야의 이름을 시드기야로 바꾸었다.

pt.L: E o rei da Babilônia fez Matanias, seu tio, rei em seu lugar, e mudou o seu nome [para] Zedequias.
pt.B: O rei da Babilônia fez Matanias, tio de Joaquim, rei no lugar dele, e mudou o seu nome para Zedequias.
pt.R: O rei da Babilônia fez Matanias, tio de Joaquim, rei no lugar dele. Ele mudou o nome de Matanias para Zedequias.

am.L: የባቢሎንም ንጉሥ አጎቱን መታንያን በእርሱ ፋንታ አነገሠው፤ ስሙንም ሴዴቅያስ ብሎ ለወጠው።
am.B: የባቢሎን ንጉሥ የዮአኪንን አጎት መታንያን በእርሱ ፋንታ አነገሠው፤ ስሙንም ለውጦ ሴዴቅያስ አለው።
am.R: የባቢሎን ንጉሥ የዮአኪንን አጎት መታንያን በእርሱ ፋንታ አነገሠው። የመታንያንም ስም ለውጦ ሴዴቅያስ አለው።

hi.L: और बाबुल के राजा ने उसके चाचा मत्तन्याह को उसके स्थान पर राजा बनाया, और उसका नाम बदलकर सिदकिय्याह रखा।
hi.B: बाबुल के राजा ने यहोयाकीन के चाचा मत्तन्याह को उसके स्थान पर राजा बनाया और उसका नाम बदलकर सिदकिय्याह रखा।
hi.R: बाबुल के राजा ने यहोयाकीन के चाचा मत्तन्याह को उसके स्थान पर राजा बनाया। उसने मत्तन्याह का नाम बदलकर सिदकिय्याह रख दिया।

ru.L: И воцарил царь Вавилона Маттанию, его дядю, вместо него, и изменил его имя на Седекия.
ru.B: Царь Вавилона воцарил вместо Иехонии его дядю Маттанию и переменил ему имя на Седекия.

uk.L: І настановив цар Вавилону царем Маттанію, його дядька, замість нього, і змінив його імʼя [на] Седекія.

decisions.choice: his uncle: Jehoiachin's father's brother
decisions.reason: Mattaniah was a son of Josiah and a brother of Jehoiakim (1 Chronicles 3:15; Jeremiah 1:3). 2 Chronicles 36:10 calls him Jehoiachin's "brother", using the word in its wider sense of a male relative.

decisions.choice: he changed his name: a sign of the overlord's power
decisions.reason: Renaming a king showed who had made him king and whom he served, as when Pharaoh Neco renamed Eliakim Jehoiakim (23:34). Mattaniah means "gift of Yahweh"; Zedekiah means "Yahweh is my righteousness" or "Yahweh is righteous". Both names honor Yahweh.

decisions.choice: Mattaniah, Zedekiah
decisions.reason: Each level keeps both names in the data's English forms. Balanced and Readable name Jehoiachin for "his" so it is clear whose uncle Mattaniah was, and Readable names Mattaniah for the second "his".

decisions.choice: "Matanías", "Sedequías"
decisions.reason: "Sedequías" as the terms note's table gives Zedekiah; "Matanías" in its usual Spanish form. Balanced and Readable name Jehoiachin, as the English does.

decisions.choice: Mattania; Sédécias
decisions.reason: Sédécias as the terms note sets; Mattania in the same transcription as the other names.

decisions.choice: baba mdogo
decisions.reason: His father's brother (meaning decision m1) is "baba mdogo" in Swahili, as in 1 Samuel; "mjomba" is a mother's brother.

decisions.choice: Matanias; Zedequias
decisions.reason: For the whole book: the king (m2) is "Zedequias", the form the shared list for Kings sets, and his first name "Matanias", the usual Brazilian form; the renaming keeps the words of 23:34.

decisions.choice: "his uncle" (dod) is "አጎቱ".
decisions.reason: "አጎት" is the everyday word for a father's brother; the meaning decision says which uncle.

decisions.choice: चाचा; मत्तन्याह, सिदकिय्याह
decisions.reason: Hindi must say which side of the family an uncle is on; the meaning decision makes him his father's brother (m1), so चाचा. Zedekiah is सिदकिय्याह, as the history-books note; Mattaniah is transcribed.

decisions.choice: "Маттания", "Седекия"
decisions.reason: The traditional Russian Bible forms; "Седекия" is the history note's form.

decisions.choice: Mattaniah "マタンヤ", Zedekiah "ツィドキヤ" (as 1CH 3 and 1KI 22)
decisions.reason: One form for this name across the books, as the 1 Chronicles notes give it for this king; many readers know ゼデキヤ, so a reviewer should confirm.

decisions.choice: the same words in Jeremiah 52:1 and in 2 Chronicles 36:11
decisions.reason: Verses 18-20 are repeated almost word for word in Jeremiah 52:1-3, which begins that book's account of Jerusalem's fall. 2 Chronicles 36:11 gives the same age and length of reign but leaves out his mother.

decisions.choice: Hamutal: the form read aloud
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) spell the name Hamital; the scribes marked Hamutal to be read aloud (qere), the form used in 23:31. It is the same woman.

decisions.choice: Hamutal daughter of Jeremiah from Libnah: also the mother of Jehoahaz
decisions.reason: Hamutal was the mother of Jehoahaz as well (23:31), so Zedekiah was his full brother and a half brother of Jehoiakim. Her father Jeremiah of Libnah, a town in the lowland of Judah, is not the prophet Jeremiah, who came from Anathoth (Jeremiah 1:1).

decisions.choice: eleven years: from 597 BC to the fall of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Zedekiah reigned until the city fell in his eleventh year (25:2), about 586 BC.

decisions.choice: Zedekiah was twenty-one years old
decisions.reason: As in verse 8: Balanced and Readable give the age as English does and put the name first.

decisions.choice: 2 Kings 24:18-25:30 is worded to be repeated in Jeremiah 52 where the Hebrew is the same.
alternatives: wording drafted separately for each book
decisions.reason: The two passages are the same account; one Amharic wording lets the reader see where they agree and where they differ.

decisions.reason: Zedekiah is compared with his brother Jehoiakim, not with his father Josiah. The book of Jeremiah shows him unwilling to heed the prophet's word even when he asked for it (Jeremiah 37-38). Jeremiah 52:2 has the same words.

decisions.reason: As in verse 9.

source.text: כִּ֣י׀עַל־אַ֣ף יְהוָ֗ה הָיְתָ֤ה בִירוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ וּבִ֣יהוּדָ֔ה עַד־הִשְׁלִכ֥וֹ אֹתָ֖ם מֵעַ֣ל פָּנָ֑יו וַיִּמְרֹ֥ד צִדְקִיָּ֖הוּ בְּמֶ֥לֶךְ בָּבֶֽל׃ס

records.literal_gloss: For on [the] anger of Yahweh it happened in Jerusalem and in Judah, until he cast them from on his face; and rebelled Zedekiah against [the] king of Babylon.

en.L: For because of the anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} it came to be in Jerusalem and in Judah, until {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} cast them out from before {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} face. And Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.
en.B: It was because of the anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} that all this happened in Jerusalem and Judah, until {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} cast them out of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} presence. And Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.
en.R: All this happened to Jerusalem and Judah because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was angry with them, until at last {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} threw them out of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} presence. Then Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.

es.L: Porque a causa de la ira {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} sucedió [esto] en Jerusalén y en Judá, hasta que los echó de delante de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} rostro. Y Sedequías se rebeló contra el rey de Babilonia.
es.B: Fue por la ira {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} que todo esto sucedió en Jerusalén y en Judá, hasta que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} los echó de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} presencia. Y Sedequías se rebeló contra el rey de Babilonia.
es.R: Todo esto les sucedió a Jerusalén y a Judá porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} estaba enojado con ellos, hasta que por fin los echó de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} presencia. Entonces Sedequías se rebeló contra el rey de Babilonia.

fr.L: Car à cause de la colère {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, cela arriva à Jérusalem et en Juda, jusqu’à ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les eût rejetés de devant {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} face. Et Sédécias se révolta contre le roi de Babylone.
fr.B: C’est à cause de la colère {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} que tout cela arriva à Jérusalem et en Juda, jusqu’à ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les rejette loin de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} présence. Et Sédécias se révolta contre le roi de Babylone.
fr.R: Tout cela est arrivé à Jérusalem et à Juda parce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} était en colère contre eux, jusqu’au jour où {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les a rejetés loin de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. Ensuite Sédécias s’est révolté contre le roi de Babylone.

sw.L: Kwa maana kwa sababu ya hasira ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ikawa hivyo katika Yerusalemu na katika Yuda, hata alipowatupa kutoka mbele ya uso {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}. Naye Sedekia akamwasi mfalme wa Babeli.
sw.B: Ilikuwa kwa sababu ya hasira ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} kwamba hayo yote yalitokea katika Yerusalemu na Yuda, mpaka alipowatupa kutoka mbele {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}. Naye Sedekia akamwasi mfalme wa Babeli.
sw.R: Hayo yote yaliipata Yerusalemu na Yuda kwa sababu {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliwakasirikia, mpaka mwishowe akawatupa kutoka mbele {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}. Kisha Sedekia akamwasi mfalme wa Babeli.

vi.L: Vì cơn giận của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} mà việc ấy xảy ra tại Giê-ru-sa-lem và Giu-đa, cho đến khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ném họ khỏi trước mặt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Sê-đê-kia nổi loạn chống lại vua Ba-by-lôn.
vi.B: Chính vì cơn giận của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} mà mọi việc ấy xảy ra tại Giê-ru-sa-lem và Giu-đa, cho đến khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ném họ ra khỏi trước mặt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Sê-đê-kia nổi loạn chống lại vua Ba-by-lôn.
vi.R: Mọi việc ấy xảy đến cho Giê-ru-sa-lem và Giu-đa vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} giận họ, cho đến cuối cùng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ném họ ra khỏi trước mặt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Rồi Sê-đê-kia nổi loạn chống lại vua Ba-by-lôn.

ko.L: 이는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 진노 때문에 예루살렘과 유다에 [이 일이] 일어났기 때문이다. 마침내 그분께서 그들을 그분의 얼굴 앞에서 내던지셨다. 그리고 시드기야가 바빌론 왕에게 반역했다.
ko.B: 이 모든 일이 예루살렘과 유다에 일어난 것은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 진노 때문이었다. 마침내 그분께서는 그들을 그분 앞에서 쫓아내셨다. 그리고 시드기야는 바빌론 왕에게 반역했다.
ko.R: 이 모든 일이 예루살렘과 유다에 일어난 것은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그들에게 노하셨기 때문이다. 마침내 그분께서는 그들을 그분 앞에서 쫓아내셨다. 그 뒤에 시드기야는 바빌론 왕에게 반역했다.

pt.L: Porque, por causa da ira {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, isso aconteceu em Jerusalém e em Judá, até que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} os lançou de diante da {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} face. E Zedequias se rebelou contra o rei da Babilônia.
pt.B: Foi por causa da ira {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} que tudo isso aconteceu em Jerusalém e em Judá, até que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} os expulsou da {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} presença. E Zedequias se rebelou contra o rei da Babilônia.
pt.R: Tudo isso aconteceu a Jerusalém e a Judá porque {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} estava irado com eles, até que por fim {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} os expulsou da {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} presença. Depois Zedequias se rebelou contra o rei da Babilônia.

am.L: ከፊቱ እስኪጥላቸው ድረስ {{divine_name:በእግዚአብሔር|በያህዌ}} ቁጣ ምክንያት በኢየሩሳሌምና በይሁዳ ላይ እንዲህ ሆነ። ሴዴቅያስም በባቢሎን ንጉሥ ላይ ዐመፀ።

am.R: ይህ ሁሉ በኢየሩሳሌምና በይሁዳ ላይ የደረሰው {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ስለ ተቆጣባቸው ነው፤ በመጨረሻም ከፊቱ አስወጥቶ ጣላቸው። ከዚያም ሴዴቅያስ በባቢሎን ንጉሥ ላይ ዐመፀ።

hi.L: क्योंकि {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} के क्रोध के कारण यरूशलेम और यहूदा में ऐसा हुआ, यहाँ तक कि उन्होंने उन्हें अपने सामने से निकाल फेंका। और सिदकिय्याह ने बाबुल के राजा से विद्रोह किया।
hi.B: {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} के क्रोध के कारण ही यरूशलेम और यहूदा में यह सब हुआ, यहाँ तक कि उन्होंने उन्हें अपने सामने से निकाल दिया। और सिदकिय्याह ने बाबुल के राजा के विरुद्ध विद्रोह किया।
hi.R: यरूशलेम और यहूदा के साथ यह सब इसलिए हुआ कि {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} उनसे क्रोधित थे, यहाँ तक कि अंत में उन्होंने उन्हें अपने सामने से बाहर फेंक दिया। तब सिदकिय्याह ने बाबुल के राजा के विरुद्ध विद्रोह किया।

ru.L: Ведь из-за гнева {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Яхве}} это было в Иерусалиме и в Иуде, пока {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} не отбросил их от своего лица. И восстал Седекия против царя Вавилона.
ru.B: Всё это произошло в Иерусалиме и Иуде из-за гнева {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Яхве}}, пока {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} не отверг их от своего лица. И Седекия восстал против царя Вавилона.
ru.R: Всё это случилось с Иерусалимом и Иудой потому, что {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}} гневался на них, пока наконец {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} не прогнал их от себя. Потом Седекия восстал против царя Вавилона.

ja.L: 実に、{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}の怒りによって、エルサレムとユダにこのことが起こり、ついに神は彼らをご自分の顔の前から投げ捨てられた。そしてツィドキヤはバビロンの王に反逆した。
ja.B: これらすべてがエルサレムとユダに起こったのは、{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}の怒りのためであり、ついに神は彼らを御前から投げ捨てられた。そして、ツィドキヤはバビロンの王に反逆した。
ja.R: これらのことがエルサレムとユダに起こったのは、{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}が人々に怒っておられたからです。そしてついに、神は人々をご自分の前から追い出されました。その後、ツィドキヤはバビロンの王に逆らいました。

uk.L: Бо через гнів {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Ягве}} сталося [це] в Єрусалимі та в Юдеї, аж поки {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} не відкинув їх від свого обличчя. І збунтувався Седекія проти царя Вавилону.
uk.B: Через гнів {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Ягве}} усе це сталося в Єрусалимі та Юдеї, аж поки {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} не відкинув їх від свого обличчя. І Седекія збунтувався проти царя Вавилону.
uk.R: Усе це сталося з Єрусалимом і Юдеєю тому, що {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Ягве}} гнівався на них, аж поки нарешті {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} не прогнав їх від свого обличчя. Тоді Седекія повстав проти царя Вавилону.

decisions.choice: because of Yahweh's anger it came to be: the events of Zedekiah's reign happened through Yahweh's anger
alternatives: Yahweh's anger was against Jerusalem and Judah
decisions.reason: The verb has no stated subject, and the sentence means that what happened in Jerusalem and Judah, the evil of its kings and the disaster that followed, came about through Yahweh's anger. It may also be read "Yahweh's anger came upon Jerusalem and Judah", with the anger itself as the subject; the sense is close.

decisions.choice: cast them out from before his face: sent them into exile out of his presence
decisions.reason: As in verse 3, to be put away from Yahweh's face is to lose the land where he had made his presence known. The same was said of Israel (17:20). Its completion is told in chapter 25.

decisions.choice: Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon: Jeremiah 52:3; 2 Chronicles 36:13
decisions.reason: Jeremiah 52:3 has the same words. 2 Chronicles 36:13 adds that Nebuchadnezzar had made him swear by God, and Ezekiel 17:13-15 calls the rebellion the breaking of a covenant oath. The rebellion leads to the siege of 25:1.

decisions.choice: all this
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "it came to be" has no stated subject; Balanced and Readable supply "all this", meaning the evil and disaster just told. Readable turns "the anger of the LORD" into "the LORD was angry with them" and adds "at last" for "until".

decisions.choice: "всё это"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "it came to be" has no stated subject; Balanced and Readable supply "всё это", the evil and disaster just told (m1). The reflexive "своего", "себя" take no deity_pronoun span where the English has "his".

decisions.choice: "ご自分の顔の前から投げ捨てられた" (L), "御前から投げ捨てられた" (B), "ご自分の前から追い出されました" (R)
decisions.reason: Cast out of his presence: sent into exile, in the words 2KI 17:23 uses.
